Sun Shine IT Solution01 · Executive summary
01 · Executive summary

A single commerce platform across web, back office and mobile

SUN SHINE IT SOLUTION proposes the design, development and deployment of a single-vendor e-commerce platform through which one business can present and sell its products online, manage its catalogue and inventory, process and fulfil customer orders, run promotions and review operational performance. The solution is delivered as three mandatory components that share one backend — a responsive e-commerce website, a centralised admin panel and backend, and a customer mobile application — with a delivery partner application available as an optional module.

What the platform does for the business

  • One catalogue, three surfaces. Products, prices, stock and offers are maintained once in the admin panel and published to both the website and the customer mobile app, so customers see consistent information wherever they shop.
  • One order pipeline. Orders placed on the website or in the mobile app arrive in the same admin queue, follow the same approved status workflow, and affect the same inventory records.
  • Operational control. Staff can review orders, update statuses, manage stock, handle cancellation and return requests, configure shipping and promotions, and restrict sensitive actions to authorised roles.
  • Visibility. Dashboards and reports are built from the data the system actually captures — orders, payments, stock movements and customer activity — so decisions are based on recorded figures rather than manual collation.
  • Room to grow. The optional delivery partner application can be added when the business is ready to manage its own last-mile delivery team.

Engagement at a glance

  • Solution type: Single-vendor e-commerce platform (not a multi-vendor marketplace)
  • Mandatory components: Website, admin panel & backend, customer mobile app
  • Optional component: Delivery partner application
  • Backend model: One shared backend and database serving all front-end surfaces
  • Mobile platform scope: Android / iOS / both — to be confirmed during requirement gathering
  • Technology stack: To be proposed and mutually approved during discovery
  • Commercials: To be completed after final scope approval
  • Timeline: To be mutually finalised after requirements and scope sign-off

Commerce you own

The storefront, data and administration remain the client's own system rather than a rented template, so catalogue structure, pricing logic, promotions and fulfilment rules can follow the business rather than the other way round.

Documented scope

Every module in this document is written as a reviewable feature list. Before development starts, each item is marked as included, optional or excluded, which keeps expectations, delivery and acceptance aligned.

Honest commitments

Features that depend on a third-party provider, paid service, business policy or client-supplied content are identified as such, so nothing is presented as committed before it has been confirmed and agreed in writing.

Scope accuracy. This document is a detailed proposed feature catalogue. Any feature that depends on business policy, a third-party provider, a paid service, special hardware or additional development must be confirmed in the final signed scope before it is treated as a committed deliverable.
Sun Shine IT Solution02 · Scope of work
02 · Scope of work

Mandatory core solution and optional add-on

The scope is divided into a mandatory base project and one clearly separated optional module. The optional module is quoted separately and is not included in the base project total unless the client selects it in writing.

Mandatory

A · E-commerce website

The customer-facing storefront for desktop, tablet and mobile browsers: catalogue browsing, search, cart, checkout, payments, accounts, order tracking and post-purchase requests, supported by policy and content pages.

Mandatory

B · Admin panel & backend

The central management system and APIs: dashboard, catalogue, inventory, orders, customers, promotions, payments, shipping, content, reports, roles and configuration — the single source of truth for all three surfaces.

Mandatory

C · Customer mobile application

A native-experience shopping app for customers covering browsing, search, cart, checkout, payment, order history, tracking, cancellation/return requests and notifications — connected to the same backend as the website.

D · Delivery partner application

Optional module

A separate application for the client's own delivery staff, covering partner login, assigned deliveries, status updates, delivery confirmation, failed-delivery reporting and delivery history, together with the matching assignment and reporting screens in the admin panel. This module is optional. It can be added if the client operates or plans to operate an in-house delivery team. It is described in full in section 06, quoted on a separate commercial line, and excluded from the mandatory base project total unless selected in writing.

Sun Shine IT Solution03 · E-commerce website
03 · Core component A

E-commerce website

Mandatory

A responsive storefront built for desktop, tablet and mobile browsers. The website is the primary discovery and purchase channel: it presents the catalogue clearly, keeps the path from product page to confirmed order short, and gives customers the self-service tools they expect after ordering. Product data, pricing, stock and promotions are read from the same backend that powers the admin panel and the mobile app, so the storefront reflects whatever the business has published centrally.

Homepage, navigation and content pages

The homepage is designed as a configurable merchandising surface rather than a fixed page, so the business can change what it promotes without development effort.

Shopping cart and order summary

Sun Shine IT Solution04 · Admin panel & backend
04 · Core component B

Admin panel and backend system

Mandatory

The admin panel is the operational centre of the platform — not a reporting screen bolted onto a storefront. It is an authenticated back-office application through which authorised staff maintain the catalogue, control inventory, process the full order lifecycle, manage customers and promotions, configure shipping and payments, publish site content and review performance. Everything the website and the customer mobile app display originates here, and every order from either channel is processed here. Roles, permissions and the exact status workflow are finalised during requirement gathering and approved before development.

B1 · Dashboard

Business overview and operational alerts

A landing view that answers the two questions staff open the system for: what needs attention now, and how the business is performing over the selected period.

  • Order statistics grouped by status for the selected period
  • Sales and revenue summaries derived from recorded order and payment data
  • Product and inventory summary, including active, inactive and low-stock counts
  • Customer statistics such as registered customers and new registrations in the period
  • Pending action queues — new orders, payment-pending orders, dispatch due, cancellation and return requests
  • Low-stock and out-of-stock alerts based on configured thresholds
  • Recent orders list with shortcuts into order detail
  • Date-range selection for the dashboard figures
  • Key indicators such as order count, order value and average order value for the selected range

All figures are calculated from data captured by this system and the configured status rules; they are not reconciled against external accounting systems.

B2 · Catalogue

Product and category management

  • Create, edit, view, duplicate, publish, unpublish and deactivate products
  • Manage product name, short and long description, specifications and image set
  • Manage regular price, sale price and effective discount display
  • Manage SKU or product reference codes where used
  • Assign products to categories and subcategories
  • Manage product variants and attributes where the variant structure is included in the approved requirements
  • Control product visibility, featured flags and display ordering
  • Manage product-level SEO fields such as URL slug, title and meta description
  • Search and filter product records by name, SKU, category, status or stock position
  • Validation of mandatory product information before publishing
  • Create, edit, reorder and deactivate categories and subcategories, with category image and description where required
  • Bulk product import and export using an agreed file format, where included in the final scope
B3 · Inventory

Stock control and availability

  • View and update stock quantity per product or per variant where variants are in scope
  • Availability status display — in stock, low stock and out of stock
  • Configurable low-stock threshold with corresponding dashboard alerts
  • Automatic inventory updates when orders are placed, cancelled or returned, following the agreed stock policy
  • Defined behaviour for orders that exceed available stock — block, warn or allow backorder, as approved
  • Manual stock adjustment with reason capture
  • Stock adjustment history and movement audit trail where included in the final scope
  • Stock position and movement reports for the selected period

Multi-warehouse stock, batch, serial or expiry tracking and procurement workflows are not included unless specifically agreed.

05 · Core component C

The customer mobile application is a committed part of this project, not a future enhancement. It gives customers a dedicated shopping channel with fast repeat ordering, saved preferences and push notifications, while running on exactly the same backend, catalogue and order pipeline as the website. A product published once, a price changed once or a stock figure updated once applies to both channels; an order placed in the app appears in the same admin queue as a website order and follows the same approved status workflow.

Shopping and account features

  • Onboarding and access: registration, login, logout and session handling using the agreed identity method, with OTP verification where a messaging provider is configured
  • Profile management: personal details, contact information and password or credential update
  • Address management: multiple saved addresses, default selection, add, edit and delete
  • Home screen: banners, promotional sections, featured products, categories and active offers, driven by the same configuration as the website
  • Catalogue browsing: categories, subcategories and product listings
  • Search, filters and sorting across supported catalogue attributes
  • Product detail screens: image gallery, description, specifications, price, discount, variants where in scope, and stock availability
  • Cart management: add, remove, update quantity and view the full charge breakdown
  • Wishlist or saved products with move-to-cart
  • Coupons and offers: apply eligible coupon codes and view applicable promotions

Platform scope — to be confirmed

The source proposal does not fix the mobile platform, so it remains an open item for requirement gathering rather than an assumption in this document.

  • Target platform: Android only, iOS only, or both — to be selected and confirmed in the final scope
  • Development approach: to be proposed during discovery and mutually approved; no specific framework or technology is assumed here
  • Supported OS versions and test devices: to be agreed before development
  • App-store publication: developer accounts, certificates, store fees, review outcomes and ongoing platform compliance are client or provider dependent

The commercial impact of the platform choice is reflected when the commercial section is completed.

Ordering, tracking and support

  • Checkout with delivery address selection and order summary showing subtotal, discount, delivery charge, taxes and payable total
  • Payment through the agreed gateway using the provider's recommended mobile flow, and Cash on Delivery where supported
  • Order confirmation screen with order reference
  • Order history with order detail screens
  • Order status and tracking information as recorded in the system
  • Cancellation and return requests according to the approved business rules
  • Push notifications for the agreed order events, where a push provider is configured and included
  • In-app customer support and contact options, such as call, email or enquiry form, routed to the agreed destination
  • Access to policy and information pages — About, FAQ, Privacy, Terms, Shipping and Return policies
  • App settings including notification preferences and logout
  • Consistent branding, typography and navigation aligned with the approved website design

How the app stays synchronised with the website

The app is a client of the same backend rather than a separate system with its own data, which is what keeps the two channels consistent.

  • Shared backend and database: the app communicates with the same APIs used by the website, so catalogue, pricing, offers, stock and customer records are read from one source
  • One customer identity: a customer can sign in on either channel with the same account and see the same addresses, order history and wishlist, subject to the approved account rules
  • One order pipeline: app orders enter the same admin order queue, consume the same inventory and follow the same configured status workflow
  • Central configuration: banners, featured products, coupons and notification events configured in the admin panel apply to the app according to the agreed display rules
  • Secure communication: API traffic over HTTPS/TLS with token-based authentication and server-side validation of every request
  • Consistent behaviour: business rules such as coupon eligibility, shipping charges, tax presentation and cancellation windows are enforced in the backend, not duplicated per channel
Confirmed during requirement gathering: mobile platform selection, supported OS versions, push notification provider, offline or caching expectations, app-store account ownership and the exact set of screens carried over from the website design.

Optional module — delivery partner application

Optional

Corresponding admin panel capabilities

Not promised in this module. Live GPS tracking, continuous background location, route optimisation, automatic nearest-partner allocation, delivery-fee or incentive calculation, partner payout management and third-party courier platform integration are not included. Sun Shine IT Solution07 · Business workflow
07 · Operations

End-to-end business workflow

The diagram and sequence below describe how the components interact from catalogue setup through to delivery and reporting. This is the proposed baseline; the exact status sequence, responsibilities and business rules are confirmed with the client during requirement gathering and approved before development begins.

1
PublishAdmin maintains catalogue, pricing, stock and offers
2
DiscoverCustomers browse on the website or mobile app
3
OrderCheckout, payment and order reference generated
4
FulfilStaff confirm, pack, dispatch and update status
5
CompleteDelivery, after-sales requests and reporting

Catalogue setup. The administrator adds and maintains products, categories, images, descriptions, pricing, stock quantities and promotional offers through the admin panel.

Publication to both channels. Published products and active offers are served through the backend to the e-commerce website and to the customer mobile application, so both channels present the same catalogue information.

Customer shopping. Customers browse or search the catalogue, review product details, add items to the cart or wishlist, apply an eligible coupon and proceed to checkout on whichever channel they prefer.

Order creation. The backend validates stock, coupon eligibility, serviceability and charge calculation, records the order with a unique reference, and updates inventory according to the agreed reservation or deduction rule.

Payment handling. For online payment, the transaction is processed through the agreed gateway and the order and payment states are set from the provider's response. For Cash on Delivery, where supported, the order is recorded with payment pending.

Administrative review. Authorised staff see the new order in the admin order queue, verify the details and move it through the approved status workflow — typically confirmed, processing and packed.

Dispatch. Staff record dispatch details and, where applicable, the courier name and tracking reference, either entered manually or received from an agreed courier integration.

Customer communication. Notifications for the configured events are sent to the customer through the channels that have been approved and configured — email, SMS, WhatsApp or push.

Customer self-service. The customer checks order status, tracking information and order history on the website or in the mobile app, and raises a cancellation or return request where the approved policy permits it.

Optional delivery assignment. If the optional delivery partner module is included, the administrator or the configured workflow assigns eligible deliveries to a delivery partner, who then updates pickup and delivery statuses from the partner app; the system reflects those updates against the order where supported.

After-sales processing. Cancellation and return requests are checked against the client-approved policy, actioned by authorised staff, and any refund is processed or recorded through the supported and agreed process.

Reporting. Management reviews recorded orders, sales, stock positions, payment outcomes and — where the optional module is included — delivery performance, using the admin panel reports for the selected period.

See also: Appendix B presents this same journey as a twenty-one step visual flow, including the payment success and failure branch.

Rules are configured, not fixed. Exact workflows depend on the final business rules, the selected integrations and the approved scope. Items such as the stock deduction point, cancellation eligibility window, refund route, invoice format and notification event list are decided during requirement gathering and then implemented as configured.
Sun Shine IT Solution08 · Technical architecture
08 · Technical approach

System architecture and integrations

The platform is proposed as a single backend serving three front-end surfaces through a shared API layer. This is the structural decision that makes the rest of the solution consistent: one catalogue, one inventory record, one customer identity and one order pipeline, regardless of where the customer shops or where staff work. The specific technology stack, frameworks, database product, cloud provider and third-party vendors are presented as subject to discovery, feasibility assessment and mutual approval, and are not assumed in this document.

Component responsibilities

  • Website frontend. Renders the catalogue, cart and checkout for browsers and handles customer account screens. It holds no business rules of its own; it requests and displays what the backend provides.
  • Customer mobile application. Provides the same shopping journey in a mobile-native experience, consuming the same APIs so that data and rules remain identical across channels.
  • Central backend and APIs. Holds the business logic — validation, pricing and charge calculation, coupon eligibility, stock rules, order state transitions and permission checks — and exposes it through a documented API layer.
  • Admin panel. The authenticated management interface over the same backend, with every action subject to role-based permission checks.
  • Database and data management. Stores catalogue, inventory, customer, order, payment, promotion, content and configuration data under a structure designed during the technical design phase, with product images and documents in the agreed storage location.
  • Authentication and authorisation. Separate identity handling for customers, administrative staff and — if the optional module is selected — delivery partners, each with its own permitted actions.

Environment and operations

  • Hosting and deployment. The application is deployed to the agreed production environment. The hosting plan, server specification, domain and SSL arrangements are confirmed during planning; provisioning, subscription and renewal remain the client's commercial responsibility unless otherwise agreed.
  • Environments. Use of separate development, testing or staging environments is proposed where the agreed hosting arrangement supports it, so that releases can be verified before reaching production.
  • Configuration management. Environment-specific settings and third-party credentials are configured securely in the deployment environment rather than embedded in distributed code.
  • Backup and recovery. Database and file backup frequency, retention period and restoration responsibility are defined with the hosting scope; where backup tooling is provided by the hosting platform, configuration support is included to the extent agreed.
  • Monitoring and maintenance. Basic application error logging is included. Uptime monitoring, alerting and ongoing maintenance activity depend on the support terms agreed commercially.
  • Scalability considerations. The architecture separates front-end surfaces from the backend so that capacity can be increased as volumes grow; actual capacity depends on the hosting plan selected by the client.

Sun Shine IT Solution09 · Security, quality & performance
09 · Engineering standards

Security, quality and performance considerations

The practices below describe how the solution will be built and verified. They are implementation commitments about process and technique, not guarantees of a particular uptime figure, certification or absolute security outcome.

Application security

  • Secure authentication for customers, administrative staff and — if selected — delivery partners
  • Role-based authorisation checks enforced on the server for every protected action
  • Password hashing and the agreed password policy; credentials never stored in readable form
  • Session and token handling with expiry according to the approved rules
  • Application secrets and provider credentials held in environment configuration, not in distributed source
  • HTTPS/TLS for deployed environments, subject to a valid certificate being available
  • Server-side input validation and output handling to mitigate common web application vulnerabilities such as injection and cross-site scripting
  • Payment handled through the gateway's recommended flow, so card data is processed by the provider rather than stored by the application
  • Customer data handled according to the agreed privacy policy and restricted to authorised screens and roles

Quality assurance

  • Functional testing of catalogue, cart, checkout, order processing and administrative workflows
  • Integration testing of payment, notification and any agreed courier or map services, in provider test mode where available
  • Order and inventory workflow testing, including cancellation, return and stock adjustment paths
  • Responsive and cross-device testing on the agreed browsers, screen sizes and devices
  • Mobile application testing on the agreed platforms and test devices
  • Negative and edge-case testing — validation failures, payment failure, out-of-stock and session expiry
  • Permission testing to confirm restricted actions are unavailable to unauthorised roles
  • Defect logging, prioritisation and retesting against the approved scope

Performance & reliability

  • Image optimisation and appropriate asset sizing for web and mobile delivery
  • Minification and caching of static assets where the hosting environment supports it
  • Database indexing and query review for catalogue, search and order listing screens
  • Pagination or incremental loading on large listings rather than unbounded result sets
  • Performance checks on key journeys — home, listing, product detail, cart and checkout
  • Structured error handling with operational logging to support diagnosis
  • Database backup planning agreed with the hosting scope, including frequency and retention
  • Graceful handling of third-party service failures so that a provider outage produces a clear message rather than an unrecoverable state
What is not claimed. This proposal does not claim any security certification, penetration-test attestation, guaranteed uptime percentage, guaranteed page-load figure or absolute protection against all threats. Measurable service levels, independent security audits and formal compliance programmes can be discussed and scoped separately if the client requires them.
Sun Shine IT Solution10 · Implementation phases
10 · Delivery approach

Project implementation phases

The project is delivered in structured phases with a defined output at the end of each one, so progress is visible and approvals happen at the right moments. Durations and dates are deliberately left blank: they are mutually finalised after requirements, integrations, mobile platform selection and scope have been approved.

Phase 01Requirement gathering

Detailed discussion of business workflows, catalogue structure, pricing and tax presentation, shipping model, payment methods, cancellation and return policy, notification events, user roles and reporting needs.

Deliverable: documented requirement summary and confirmed business rules.

Phase 02Scope confirmation & planning

Each feature in this proposal is marked as included, optional or excluded. Integrations, mobile platform scope and client responsibilities are fixed, and the project plan and approval checkpoints are agreed.

Deliverable: signed-off scope document and project plan with the mutually agreed schedule.

Phase 03UI/UX design & approval

Design of the key website screens, admin panel layouts and mobile app screens in line with the approved branding, followed by a review and revision cycle within the agreed limits.

Deliverable: approved screen designs forming the visual baseline for development.

Phase 04Backend & admin panel development

Database design, core business logic, API layer and the admin modules — catalogue, inventory, orders, customers, promotions, shipping, content, reports, roles and configuration.

Deliverable: working backend and admin panel on the development environment.

Phase 05Website development

Implementation of the approved storefront designs and the complete customer journey — catalogue, search, cart, checkout, accounts, order tracking and content pages — against the backend APIs.

Deliverable: functional e-commerce website on the development environment.

Phase 06Customer mobile app development

Implementation of the mobile application for the confirmed platform(s), covering onboarding, browsing, search, cart, checkout, payment, order history, tracking, requests and notifications.

Deliverable: installable test build of the customer application.

Phase 07Optional delivery module If selected

Carried out only if the optional delivery partner application is selected: partner app development plus the delivery assignment, monitoring and reporting screens in the admin panel.

Deliverable: test build of the delivery partner app and the related admin screens.

Phase 08Integration & configuration

Connection and configuration of the agreed payment gateway, notification channels and any approved courier, map or analytics services, using credentials supplied by the client.

Deliverable: integrated services verified in test mode where the provider supports it.

Phase 09Testing & quality assurance

Functional, integration, workflow, responsive, cross-device and mobile testing, followed by defect resolution against the approved scope.

Deliverable: tested build with the defect log addressed to the agreed criteria.

Phase 10User acceptance testing

Client review against the approved scope, consolidated feedback within the agreed review period and resolution of reproducible in-scope defects.

Deliverable: UAT feedback log and client acceptance confirmation.

Phase 11Deployment & production setup

Release to the agreed production hosting environment, domain and SSL configuration where access is provided, production configuration of integrations and submission of the mobile app(s) to the selected store(s) where included.

Deliverable: live platform and submitted application builds.

Phase 12Training, documentation & handover

Administrator walkthrough of the admin panel and operational workflows, together with handover of the agreed documentation, credentials and source code as specified in the final contract.

Deliverable: training session and the agreed handover package.

Phase 13Post-launch support

Support for the launched platform strictly according to the warranty or support terms agreed commercially, covering reproducible in-scope defects.

Deliverable: support as per the agreed terms; duration and coverage to be completed in the commercial section.

12 · Verification & go-live

Testing, acceptance, deployment and handover

This section sets out how the solution is verified before launch, what the client needs to provide for deployment, and how the project is formally accepted and handed over.

Testing performed before handover

  • Functional testing of catalogue browsing, search, filters, product detail, cart, checkout and account management
  • Order and inventory workflow testing covering order creation, status transitions, stock deduction, cancellation, return and restocking per the agreed rules
  • Payment workflow testing for success, failure, pending and cancelled states in the provider's test mode where available, plus the COD path where included
  • Integration testing of notification channels and any approved courier, map or analytics services
  • Responsive and cross-device testing on the agreed browsers, screen sizes and devices
  • Mobile application testing on the agreed platforms and test devices, including install, login, ordering and notification paths
  • Permission and role testing to confirm restricted actions are correctly limited
  • Defect resolution for reproducible in-scope defects, prioritised and retested before handover

Client inputs required for deployment

  • Production hosting environment with the required access, or approval of the arrangement agreed for provisioning it
  • Domain control and SSL certificate arrangement
  • Live credentials for the payment gateway and any other approved third-party services
  • App-store developer accounts and signing assets for the mobile platform(s) in scope
  • Final approved content — policy pages, product data, images and branding assets
  • Nominated client contacts for UAT, approvals and go-live sign-off
  • Timely approvals at each defined checkpoint

Deployment dates depend on these inputs being available; delays in access or approvals shift the schedule correspondingly.

User acceptance and final acceptance

  • The client tests the delivered solution against the approved scope during the agreed UAT window
  • Feedback is consolidated through the nominated contact and logged in a single list
  • Reproducible defects within the approved scope are corrected and retested
  • Items identified as new functionality are handled through the change request process rather than as defects
  • Acceptance criteria, review period and defect classification are agreed before UAT begins
  • Final acceptance is recorded against the mutually agreed requirements and deliverables

Deployment, training and handover

  • Release of the approved build to the production environment
  • Production configuration of integrations, notification templates and store settings
  • Submission of the mobile application(s) to the selected store(s) where included in scope; store review outcomes and timelines are controlled by the platform owners
  • Administrator walkthrough covering day-to-day operations in the admin panel
  • Handover of the agreed documentation, credentials and source code per the final contract
  • Confirmation of backup, monitoring and support arrangements to the extent included in the agreed hosting and support scope
Included work versus separate agreement. Development, testing, deployment, training and handover for the approved scope are included in this proposal. Ongoing maintenance, hosting administration, content population on the client's behalf, marketing activity, new feature development after acceptance and third-party subscription costs are not included and require a separate agreement.

C · Third-party services and subscriptions

An e-commerce platform depends on several external services that are purchased from their own providers rather than built by us. These are charged on the providers' own rates and renewal cycles, so they sit outside the one-time development cost above and outside the annual maintenance charge in section D.

These services can be arranged in either of two ways, and GGSS can choose a different option for each service — for example hold the domain itself while asking us to provide and manage the server.

Option 1 · Default

GGSS holds its own accounts

  • GGSS purchases each service directly in its own name and owns the account
  • The provider invoices GGSS, and GGSS pays and renews the subscription
  • GGSS shares the credentials with us so we can configure and integrate
  • SUN SHINE IT SOLUTION charges nothing in this category — these costs sit entirely on the client side
  • GGSS keeps full ownership and control of every account from day one

This is the model assumed in this proposal and in the exclusions listed in section 14.

Option 2 · Managed by us

SUN SHINE IT SOLUTION provides and manages

  • We procure the service — the server or hosting, and any other item from the table below — and configure it
  • GGSS does not open an account with that provider and does not pay the provider at all. The provider invoices us, not GGSS, so the cost does not sit on the client side
  • We handle setup, management, monitoring and renewal for as long as the arrangement runs
  • GGSS pays one consolidated managed-service charge to SUN SHINE IT SOLUTION instead of several provider bills
  • That charge is different from the provider's own rate, because it also covers procurement, configuration, management and renewal handling on your behalf

Quoted on its own commercial line. It is separate from the one-time development cost and separate from the annual maintenance charge in section D.

Sun Shine IT SolutionAppendix A · System architecture
Appendix A · Reference diagram

System architecture and platform overview

This diagram is a visual companion to section 08. It shows the whole platform on one sheet: the customer-facing surfaces on the left, the backend services and data layer in the centre, the external services the platform connects to, the administration modules on the right, and the five operational flows that run through them — customer journey, order processing, inventory, shipping and payment. The infrastructure band at the bottom illustrates how such a platform is typically deployed on a cloud environment.

How to read this diagram

  • Left — customer surfaces. The website and the customer mobile application both talk to the same backend. Every action a customer can take is listed against them, which is why the catalogue, prices and order history stay identical on either channel.
  • Centre — backend and data. The business logic modules sit around a single application server, which reads and writes one database and one file store. This is the single source of truth referred to throughout the proposal.
  • Centre-right — external services. Payment gateway, courier API, email, SMS and push notification providers. These are the third-party services priced separately in section 13 C.
  • Right — admin panel. The thirteen management modules described in section 04, each operating on the same backend rather than on a copy of the data.
  • Middle band — five operational flows. The order, inventory, shipping and payment sequences that the status workflow in section 04 B5 controls.
  • Bottom band — infrastructure. DNS, CDN, load balancing, security, hosting, managed database, cache, storage, background jobs, monitoring, secrets and backups.

Important note on this diagram

The product and vendor names shown inside the diagram — the cloud platform, database engine, payment gateways, courier services, messaging providers and supporting tools — are illustrative examples of the kind of service each box represents. They are not a committed technology selection.

As stated in section 08 and section 14, the actual technology stack, hosting provider, database product and every third-party vendor are proposed during discovery, assessed for feasibility and cost, and confirmed with GGSS in writing before development starts.

The structure shown here — one backend serving three surfaces, one database, one order pipeline, role-controlled administration — is the part this proposal commits to.

Sun Shine IT SolutionAppendix B · Customer journey
Appendix B · Reference diagram

Complete customer journey — website and mobile app

This diagram is a visual companion to section 07. It follows a single customer through all twenty-one steps of a purchase, from opening the website or the mobile application to delivery, post-purchase actions and a repeat order. The screen sketches show the sort of interface each step presents, so the business team can review the journey without reading a specification.

What the journey shows

  • Steps 1–6 — discovery to account. Visit, browse and search, product detail, add to cart or wishlist, checkout entry, and login, registration or guest checkout where that rule is enabled.
  • Steps 7–12 — checkout. Delivery address, shipping method, coupon application, order summary with the full charge breakdown, payment method selection and payment.
  • Step 13 — the payment decision point. The diamond shows the branch this proposal describes in section 03 A6: a successful payment creates the order, while a failed payment offers retry or an alternative method and does not create an order.
  • Steps 14–17 — fulfilment. Order confirmation with notifications, verification and stock check, picking, quality check, packing, shipping label and handover to the courier.
  • Steps 18–21 — delivery and after-sales. Out for delivery, delivery confirmation, review, return or exchange and customer support, then the repeat purchase loop.

Important note on this diagram

The products, screen designs, amounts, currency symbols, coupon values, order and tracking identifiers shown in the diagram are sample placeholders used to illustrate the flow. They are not the proposed visual design, the proposed catalogue or any pricing commitment.

The actual screen design is produced and approved in the UI/UX phase, and the currency, tax presentation, shipping rules, coupon rules, cancellation window and payment methods are configured to GGSS's confirmed business rules, as recorded in sections 03, 04 and 14.

The sequence of steps and the decision points are what this diagram is intended to communicate.
